note: The queued story's data (92% of chains, 3.5M->3.0M cashier jobs 2013-2023, 4% vs 1.6% loss), retold to the channel's current narration rules: one number a beat, said in words, what it means, a closing that says why you care.
lines: Self-checkout was sold as the future. Now it's quietly costing stores a fortune.
Nine out of ten big grocery chains now have self-checkout, so the lanes you grew up with are disappearing.
That's half a million cashier jobs gone in ten years, the people who used to scan your groceries and say hi.
And here's the twist. Stores lose more than twice as much at self-checkout as they do at a real register.
So the machine took the job, and it's still losing the money. The line moved. So did the job.
